questions.question: Given matrix A with dimensions 2 x 3 and matrix B with dimensions 2 x 2, why is the product AB undefined while the product BA is defined?
options: AB is undefined because the number of columns in A (3) does not equal the number of rows in B (2), while BA is defined because the number of columns in B (2) equals the number of rows in A (2).
AB is undefined because the number of rows in A (2) does not equal the number of columns in B (2), while BA is defined because matrix multiplication must always proceed in alphabetical order.
AB is undefined because A has more columns than rows, while BA is defined because B is a square matrix.
AB is undefined because the number of columns in A (3) does not equal the number of columns in B (2), while BA is defined because both matrices have 2 rows.
questions.answer: AB is undefined because the number of columns in A (3) does not equal the number of rows in B (2), while BA is defined because the number of columns in B (2) equals the number of rows in A (2).

questions.question: According to the general rule for multiplying an m x n matrix A and an n x p matrix B, what are the dimensions of the product matrix C = AB, and how is its entry cij defined?
options: C is an m x p matrix, and cij is the product of the ith row of A and the jth column of B.
C is an n x n matrix, and cij is the product of the ith column of A and the jth row of B.
C is an m x p matrix, and cij is the product of the jth row of A and the ith column of B.
C is a p x m matrix, and cij is the product of the ith row of A and the jth column of B.
questions.answer: C is an m x p matrix, and cij is the product of the ith row of A and the jth column of B.
